method: Reproduced the seven reviewer conditions against operability.v2 and confirmed that the old checker accepted deleted gates, decorative schemas, imaginary qualification, and contradictory identity/budget prose.
Traced every threat property into the live threat-model artifact and every gate subject into a closed required-property registry.
Separated architecture implementability, harness qualification, and release demonstration; no boolean or implementable test declaration is release evidence.
Replaced prose-only event, projection, audit, and capacity contracts with typed fixtures and added eleven checker mutations for the original defect classes.

findingDispositions.evidence: The prior gate list was not exhaustive, deletion of G1 through G11 escaped, and no closed property-to-gate relation existed.
findingDispositions.reasoning: A release rule cannot quantify over an unstated property universe. The registry and same-subject gate join must be executable.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Add a closed requiredPropertyRegistry, exact source/subject/gate mappings, and a derived releaseDecision.
findingDispositions.verification: OP-TM and OP-REL validate 25 exact properties and 19 live gates; delete-property, delete-gate, wrong-subject, and false-release mutations are rejected. G19 prevents storage admission from masquerading as resolution of V10.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A different closed registry that is mechanically derived from all normative source contracts and produces the same release decision.

findingDispositions.evidence: The former prose simultaneously required ExecutionId and Run budgets universally while declaring those identities absent before admission/seal.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Correlation and budget identity are phase properties, not global event fields.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Define request-validation, admitted-attempt, sealed-attempt, and stored-read phases with exact identity and budget owners.
findingDispositions.verification: Seven event fixtures include pre-admission and post-seal positive and negative cases; identity/budget phase mutations are rejected by OP-ID.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A lifecycle in which ExecutionId and RunId are allocated before request validation without changing D9/C-2 identity semantics.

findingDispositions.evidence: G12 named eight checkers, asserted observedFailure=true without evidence, and overclaimed architecture coherence.
findingDispositions.reasoning: A retained design-checker suite proves only the exact checks and mutations it executed; it cannot qualify product behavior or semantic framing.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Enumerate the exact twelve contract checkers, keep completeness separate, narrow G12, and leave it IMPLEMENTABLE until evidence exists.
findingDispositions.verification: OP-QUAL checks the exact suite and forbids paper qualification; suite deletion and fake evidence mutations fail. The register title is updated to avoid a stale gate count.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A retained meta-run record tied to immutable checker digests could later move G12 to QUALIFIED, but would not broaden its subject.

findingDispositions.evidence: Projection parity was prose, arbitrary fields passed, and SARIF Coverage loss was unnecessary because SARIF property bags support extensions.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Human, CI, and agent clients require one canonical semantic record with explicitly typed projections; renderer convenience cannot erase evidence fields.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Define seven canonical fields, five surface mappings, canonical Run fixtures, permitted display-only losses, and lossless SARIF property-bag retention.
findingDispositions.verification: Seven projection fixtures span pass/fail/indeterminate, truncation, artifacts, and IDs; field and SARIF-loss mutations fail OP-PAR.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A normative SARIF constraint forbidding custom property bags; no such constraint was found in SARIF 2.1.

findingDispositions.evidence: Only runtime capability denial lacks a selected mechanism. Static core closure and provider crash containment have concrete build/fault-injection targets.
findingDispositions.reasoning: The review is correct about splitting targets. The initial product must also exclude every feature that depends on G9, so G9 does not become a hidden week-one fork.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Keep G9 BLOCKED-NO-MECHANISM; split G10 static closure and G11 provider containment with implementable targets; reject capability-dependent initial-product plans.
findingDispositions.verification: OP-QUAL enforces G9/G10/G11 states and targets. DELIVERY admission rejects imperative, Probe, untrusted, scenario-effectful, and network-granted modes until ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT exists.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A selected restricted runtime with escape tests would make G9 implementable and permit reconsidering the excluded features.

findingDispositions.evidence: The old audit plane had no typed record, ordering, atomicity, failure, rollback, concurrency, or privacy semantics.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Auditability is a host transaction protocol; a field list cannot resolve crash or concurrent-mutation behavior.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Specify a closed HostAuditRecord and PREPARED/COMMITTED/ROLLBACK/RECOVERY protocol with canonical commitments, redaction, and mutation atomicity.
findingDispositions.verification: Eight fixtures cover crash-before, crash-after, concurrent mutation, rollback, purge, recovery, and redaction; audit schema/protocol mutations fail OP-AUD.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A datastore transaction model proving an equivalent event-sourced protocol with the same observable recovery states.

findingDispositions.evidence: The former reference capacity class had no repository, language, platform, hardware, or resource limits.
findingDispositions.reasoning: A performance gate without a workload and hardware floor is not falsifiable.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Define versioned reference-standard-v1 with independent memory, disk, runtime, and cancellation limits plus a measurement protocol.
findingDispositions.verification: OP-CAP validates every dimension and rejects absent workload/hardware/limit mutations; the class is explicitly a normative fallback pending measurement.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Representative measurements may replace the fallback thresholds, but only through a new versioned capacity class.

sealedPropertiesCovered: closed required-property-to-gate mapping and derived release decision
phase-aware event correlation and volume ownership
typed parity across human, JSON, SARIF, HTML, and MCP projections
knownLimitations: No product exists: 0 of 25 required properties are DEMONSTRATED and product release remains BLOCKED.
G9 has no capability-runtime mechanism; dependent features are excluded from the initial product.
G19 has no selected V10 evaluation-proof/retention mechanism; durable-authoritative retention is excluded.
reference-standard-v1 is a normative fallback, not a measured user SLO.
Some SARIF viewers may hide extension properties even though serialized SARIF retains them.

undischargedPropertyClassification.all 25 product properties: legitimate pre-implementation evidence gap; architecture gates are implementable but release evidence does not exist
undischargedPropertyClassification.runtime capability denial (G9): unresolved architecture decision; every dependent feature is excluded until its mechanism exists
undischargedPropertyClassification.durable-authoritative evidence custody (: unresolved V10 architecture decision; durable-authoritative retention is excluded until an independently verified proof/custody mechanism exists
undischargedPropertyClassification.capacity thresholds: acceptable measurement question with versioned reference-standard-v1 as the normative fallback

sealRecommendation.note: The operability architecture is buildable and mechanically guarded. This does not qualify or release a product.
sealRecommendation.consumerB: Yes for events, gates, projections, audit, and capacity contracts; implement G9-dependent modes and G19-dependent durable-authoritative retention as rejected at admission.
